title: Normative Models

description.main: A two-volume slipcased catalogue for Christopher Williams's 2018 exhibition Normative Models at the Kestner Gesellschaft, Hanover. Both volumes carry the same image sequence, one paired with Brecht's The Trial of Lucullus and the other with an essay by David Crowley.
description.extended:
A two-volume catalogue in a slipcase for Normative Models, Christopher Williams's 2018 exhibition at the Kestner Gesellschaft in Hanover, published by Walther König.

The two softcover volumes carry an identical sequence of images and differ only in their text. The first prints Bertolt Brecht's The Trial of Lucullus, and the second prints David Crowley's essay “Applied Fantastic: On the Polish Women's Magazine Ty I Ja.” Christina Végh edited the book and curated the exhibition with Lea Altner. The show ran from 5 May to 29 July 2018, and the cover names it the Kestner Gesellschaft's exhibition no. 547. It centred on seven photographs of cars, children, cookware, animals, furniture and other everyday subjects. Williams takes generic image types like these and remakes them with high production values and close attention to detail.

Williams was born in Los Angeles in 1956 and studied at the California Institute of the Arts in the late 1970s under John Baldessari, Douglas Huebler and Michael Asher. He has been Professor of Photography at the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf since 2008. His exhibitions treat display structures, graphic design, publications and press materials as part of the work.
description.artist_bio: Born 1956 in Los Angeles; studied at CalArts in the late 1970s under Baldessari, Huebler and Asher; Professor of Photography at the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf since 2008.
description.exhibition_context: Normative Models, Kestner Gesellschaft, Hanover, 5 May – 29 July 2018; curated by Christina Végh and Lea Altner.
